text:
david: heads-up — after the kernel-selector change in yesterday's deploy APAC prefix hit rate tanked ~12% vs EU/NA. seeing more cold-starts and higher p50 token latency.

sasha: uhoh. which change specifically? the hash normalization patch?

david: yeah, the `hash-salt` normalization we added to make kernel selection deterministic across machines. it altered cache key canonicalization for some multi-prompt prefixes.

ken: do we have a repro profile? can we see the exact key diffs?

david: pushed a quick diff of sample keys to the perf bucket, but quick snapshot here:

```
region APAC | prefix_hit 0.73 -> 0.61
region EU   | prefix_hit 0.86 -> 0.85
region NA   | prefix_hit 0.88 -> 0.87
p50 tokens  | 28ms -> 37ms (APAC)
sample keys (old -> new):
  "prompt|user:42|ctx" -> "prompt|user:42|ctx|salted"
  "system|v1|x"       -> "system|v1|x|norm"
```

maria: interesting — looks like normalization appended tokens for some canonical paths, which breaks existing KV entries. that explains replication mismatches.

ken: does replication use the raw key or a normalized key?

david: runtime uses normalized key for local cache, but replication pipeline was still sending raw keys. so APAC nodes primed with raw keys never match local normalized lookups.

sasha: so two issues: keying divergence + kernel dispatch variance. both happened in same deploy. :(

infra-bot: incident created: INC-APAC-PRFX-209876 (priority: high)

maria: mitigation options:
- revert normalization in kernel-selector promptly (fast rollback)
- add transient aliasing: check raw-key then normalized-key for lookup (cheap fix)
- force regional re-prime job to rebuild KV with normalized keys (longer)

ken: aliasing seems safest short-term. we can add a dual-lookup path: first try normalized, then fallback to legacy raw key. cheap perf hit but avoids rollback.

david: agreed. i prototyped dual-lookup in a canary: added `kv.get(key_norm) || kv.get(key_raw)` in the runtime path. p95 latency +1ms on canary but hit rate restored to ~0.82 in APAC.

sasha: nice. what's the rollout plan?

maria: plan: 1) ship dual-lookup to host pool in canary APAC (1 host) + monitor 2) if stable for 30m, expand to 10% 3) simultaneously trigger re-replicate job to populate normalized keys 4) revert dual-lookup after re-replication completes (~24h)

ken: a couple of follow-ups:
- ensure replication coordinator tags source tag so we don't thrash on re-replication (use epoch id)
- add a metric: `kv_key_variant_mismatch` (raw vs norm) to monitor ongoing churn

infra-bot: deploy queued: build/rt-dual-lookup@sha-abc123 -> stage -> canary-apac

david: note: batching heuristics also interacted — kernel-selector change nudged some long-context requests onto a different kernel, which changes sequence lengths and therefore batching windows. that amplified cost of extra lookups.

sasha: any visible token cost delta?

david: small: +3% token CPU in APAC canaries during peak. acceptable short-term given hit-rate gains.

maria: OK. i'll run the re-replicate with `--epoch=209876` and a low RPS priming profile: `wrk -t4 -c50 -d600s --script priming.lua` to rebuild with normalized keys. we'll throttle to avoid saturation.

ken: and add a quick kernel-selection toggle flag in runtime config so we can flip back if other regressions show up. feature-flag: `kernel.norm.enable` default false.

david: will add the flag and update observability (trace label `keying.variant`).

maria: timeline: deploy dual-lookup canary in 10m, monitor 60m. re-replicate start in 2h, expect finish ~24h.

sasha: thanks — also capture this in the postmortem template (link to perf traces + key samples). adding to incident. :thumbsup:
